subject: Re: Order Form — Indemnity reciprocity, export-control & training-data carveouts
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily@helixcloud.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixcloud.io, Tom Wu <tom.wu@helixcloud.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Indemnity carveouts & export-control exception request

Jordan —

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement and legal at HelixCloud reviewed the indemnity sections and we need to ask for three narrow carveouts before we can proceed to signature:

1) Reciprocity / mutuality — we can’t accept broad mutual indemnity for model training or outputs that are not tied to Redwood’s negligence. Can Redwood limit customer indemnity to claims arising from customer-provided data or customer modifications?

2) Export-control / sanctions exception — we need an explicit carveout so that HelixCloud is not on the hook for exports or outputs restricted by government controls (especially AI model outputs that may include dual-use content).

3) Training-data exclusions — if HelixCloud shares datasets (PII, licensed corpora) for fine-tuning, we want a clear promise that Redwood won’t assert IP claims against us for that material and that any third-party claim tied to our supplier-provided data stays with Redwood.

Attached is a short note from procurement highlighting the ask and a proposed redline template (PDF). Would appreciate a strawman or proposed language by early next week — our procurement window closes 10/08.

Can we schedule a 30-min call with legal to walk through?

Best,
Emily Stone
Head of Legal Ops — HelixCloud
emily@helixcloud.io

Attachment: Helix-Redline-Reqs.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Tom Wu <tom.wu@helixcloud.io>, procurement@helixcloud.io
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Indemnity carveouts & export-control exception request

Emily — thanks for the clear note and the PDF. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (AE) so we can put a concise compromise on paper. High-level thinking from my side:

- Reciprocity: Redwood is willing to narrow customer indemnity where appropriate; we typically ask for indemnity when customer data or inputs cause third-party claims or where customer violates use restrictions. We cannot broadly waive indemnity for customer-caused infringement.
- Export-control carveout: I think a narrowly scoped exception that excludes government-authorized claims (sanctions/export restrictions) is reasonable — need Kimberly to confirm wording.
- Training-data: we can clarify that Redwood won’t assert IP against customer for materials they provided, and we can add a process for flags / provenance. We will need to discuss how this interacts with our model-improvement program and whether data is used for aggregate training.

Kimberly/Karthik — can legal provide two options: (A) minimal language that addresses Helix’s asks and (B) a more protective Redwood-friendly proposal with a fallback compromise? Procurement deadline 2026-10-08; happy to take this to a short call.

I’ve attached Helix’s PDF into our folder and marked as "priority".

Thanks —
Jordan Blake

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Stone <emily@helixcloud.io>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@helixcloud.io>, procurement@helixcloud.io
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Indemnity carveouts & export-control exception request

Team / Emily —

Thanks for the asks. I reviewed HelixCloud’s note and drafted a short set of proposed redlines and alternative compromise language (attached: JK_Proposed_Redlines.docx). Key points and risk positions below:

1) Reciprocity / mutuality
- Risk: broad mutual indemnities create open-ended exposure for both parties and are often challenged by insurance teams.
- Recommendation: Customer indemnity should be limited to claims arising from: (i) customer-provided data that infringes third-party rights; (ii) Customer’s negligence or willful misconduct; or (iii) customer modifications to Redwood services that materially cause infringement.
- Sample language snippet (suggested compromise): "Customer will indemnify Redwood for third-party claims to the extent such claims arise directly from Customer-supplied data or Customer’s unauthorized modification of the Services. Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that Redwood-provided Model Outputs infringe a third party’s intellectual property, provided such claims do not arise from Customer-supplied training data or Customer instructions that intentionally induce infringing outputs."

2) Export-control / sanctions exception
- Recommendation: Add a narrowly tailored carveout: neither party shall be required to perform or indemnify for obligations to the extent compliance with applicable export controls or sanctions would be violated.
- Suggest: cross-reference an exceptions clause and include a process for notice and mitigation.

3) Training-data exclusions / model improvement
- We can commit not to assert IP rights over Customer-provided datasets used solely for Customer’s private fine-tuning (i.e., we won’t claim ownership or assert IP rights back against HelixCloud).
- However, if Customer opts into Redwood’s model-improvement program (data used to improve shared models), we need express consent and limited license terms; we should also maintain an indemnity carveout for claims tied to Customer-supplied third-party licensed content.

4) Defense control & settlement
- Helix is likely to push back on Redwood "defend and control" language. Our preference is to defend and control with cooperation obligations; if Helix wants to retain control we should include a carve-out that any settlement that admits liability or imposes non-monetary obligations requires Redwood’s consent.

5) Liability cap interaction
- Propose any indemnity for IP infringement be subject to the monetary cap in the order form (subject to carveouts for willful misconduct as usual).

Next steps I propose: (a) share the two-tier redline (attached), (b) run quick legal-to-legal call (20–30 min) to agree language, (c) finalize order form for signature. I’ve attached redlines and a short memo on why the compromise balances Helix’s procurement needs with Redwood’s exposure.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Indemnity carveouts & export-control exception request

Kimberly / Jordan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the compromise language. A few quick points from HelixCloud legal: 

- The proposed defense-and-control with consent carveout is workable only if we have visibility into Redwood’s defense strategy and if Helix can veto any settlement that imposes ongoing operational constraints (e.g., takedown that affects our production).
- For export-controls, please add an explicit reference to "applicable law including U.S. export controls and sanctions" so our audit/compliance folks can accept it.
- On training-data: we like the "no assertion of IP rights" promise for private fine-tuning. For any data used in Redwood’s shared model program, Helix needs the ability to revoke consent and a data deletion window.

We are happy to take a quick legal-to-legal call. Tom and I are available Monday 10/05 10:00–11:30 PT or Tuesday 10/06 13:00–15:00 PT. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Emily Stone
HelixCloud — Legal Ops

Team — quick recap and proposed next steps before our legal call:

1) Kimberly will present Option A (minimal carveouts) and Option B (Redwood-favorable + fallback).
2) Proposed mutual language items: export-control reference to "applicable law (including U.S. export controls and sanctions)"; training-data revocation process and 30-day deletion SLA for shared-model consent revocation.
3) Defense control: Kimberly recommends "Redwood will defend and control the defense subject to Customer cooperation; any settlement that imposes ongoing obligations requires mutual written consent" — Helix is asking for veto on operationally impactful settlements.
4) Financials: indemnity exposure will sit behind the Order Form cap, except for claims resulting from willful misconduct.

Call scheduling: Emily, we can do Monday 10/05 at 10:30 PT (Jordan, Kimberly, Karthik, Marcus attending). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.
